ADU218 invalid / out-of-range command transcript
===============================================
Device: Ontrak ADU218, USB 0a07:00da
State:  all relays OPEN throughout; none of these changed relay state
Read timeout: 2000 ms; the ioctl itself raises OSError errno 110.

Headline finding: an ADU218 answers a command it does not understand
with SILENCE - no error string, no sentinel. So a driver cannot learn
at runtime whether a response is due; it needs a per-command table.

Mitigating half: the session is NOT poisoned. The next valid command
answers normally, with no re-claim, re-open or power cycle. Unlike the
SDM4065A, where an undefined header can strand the endpoints
(KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md section F-8).

=== COMMAND THE MANUAL'S SUMMARY TABLE INVENTS ===
# RI is listed in section 5 but the function is called PI in 6b.
# A valid command is sent immediately after, to show recovery.
RI       -> TIMEOUT (errno 110)
PI       -> b'\x01000\x00\x00\x00\x00'         payload='000'    len=3

=== OUTRIGHT GARBAGE ===
XYZ      -> TIMEOUT (errno 110)
PK       -> b'\x01000\x00\x00\x00\x00'         payload='000'    len=3
(empty)  -> TIMEOUT (errno 110)
PK       -> b'\x01000\x00\x00\x00\x00'         payload='000'    len=3

=== VALID VERB, OUT-OF-RANGE INDEX ===
# Eight relays (K0..K7), four lines per input port (0..3), eight counters.
RPK8     -> TIMEOUT (errno 110)
RPK9     -> TIMEOUT (errno 110)
RPA4     -> TIMEOUT (errno 110)
RPB4     -> TIMEOUT (errno 110)
RE8      -> TIMEOUT (errno 110)
PK       -> b'\x01000\x00\x00\x00\x00'         payload='000'    len=3

=== TRUNCATED / MALFORMED ARGUMENTS ===
RPK      -> TIMEOUT (errno 110)
MK       -> TIMEOUT (errno 110)
MK9999   -> TIMEOUT (errno 110)
DB9      -> TIMEOUT (errno 110)
PK       -> b'\x01000\x00\x00\x00\x00'         payload='000'    len=3

=== WRITE-ONLY COMMANDS PRODUCE NO RESPONSE EITHER ===
# Silence here is CORRECT, not an error, and is indistinguishable on
# the wire from the invalid-command case above. That is precisely why
# the driver needs an explicit 'expects a response' flag per command.
RK0      -> (sent; no response expected, nothing read)
MK000    -> (sent; no response expected, nothing read)
DB1      -> (sent; no response expected, nothing read)

=== NOT EXERCISED HERE, DELIBERATELY ===
# WD1/WD2/WD3 arm the hardware watchdog, which resets all relays on
# timeout. Arming it during characterisation would make every later
# reading depend on how fast the next command arrived. Watchdog
# behaviour belongs in the simulator and in a separately scoped
# hardware test.
